Theorem
[Pinching estimate for the smallest curvature eigenvalue] Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0271, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0272, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0273 1. Theorem 9.4\group positive-section-dominates

Let $(\mathcal M^3,g(t))$ be any solution of the Ricci flow on a closed $3$-manifold for $0\le t<T$. Let $ u (x,t)$ denote the smallest eigenvalue of the curvature operator. If $\inf _{x\in \mathcal M^3} u (x,0)\ge -1$, then at any point $(x,t)\in \mathcal M^3 imes [0,T)$ where $ u (x,t)<0$, the scalar curvature satisfies \[ R\ge | u | igl(\log | u |+\log (1+t)-3 igr). \]

Proof

Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0271, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0272, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0273 \sketch The source first establishes two convexity lemmas: a time-dependent convex cone of curvature operators and a differential inequality for the quantity $\Omega = r (\mathbb P)/(- u (\mathbb P))-\log (- u (\mathbb P))$. These are then combined with the maximum principle for systems to show that the curvature operator remains in the cone for as long as $ u <0$. The claimed scalar-curvature lower bound follows by rewriting the cone condition in terms of $R= r \Rm $ and $ u $.

□
